players.name: Brayden Point
players.inj_detail: Left the Nov 8 game at Winnipeg after six shifts in the first period with an undisclosed injury and did not return. Coach Jon Cooper said he hopes it isn't serious but that Point might miss some time; no timeline has been given and Daily Faceoff lists him as day-to-day.

players.name: Ivan Demidov
players.inj_detail: Lower-body injury listed Oct 3, on injured reserve since Oct 6. He has skated and could rejoin team practice as early as this week, per RDS on Nov 4.

players.name: William Eklund
players.inj_detail: Ankle injury listed Oct 8. He is expected to miss 10 to 12 weeks.

players.name: Dylan Larkin
players.note: Suspended by Red Wings until traded

players.name: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins
players.inj_detail: Took a puck to the side of the head in the Nov 7 game against Vancouver and did not finish the game. No timeline has been reported.

players.name: Anthony Mantha
players.inj_detail: Took a high stick to the throat in the Nov 7 overtime win over the Islanders and did not return. Coach Sheldon Keefe said Nov 8 he will miss some time, with the extent not yet known.

players.name: Mathew Barzal
players.inj_detail: Knee injury listed Sep 16. He returned to practice in a non-contact jersey on Nov 4, with no return date reported.

players.name: Bowen Byram
players.inj_detail: Upper-body injury listed Oct 15. He was placed on injured reserve Nov 3.

recap.text: PhilCap and Tage Against the Machine share the real-standings lead at 182 points each, with 97 Problems 5 back at 177 and Debits & Checks on 176.
recap.impact: We're 5th with 174, just 8 off the lead. It's close enough that the real standings don't matter much yet; the projections tell the bigger story.

recap.text: Lord of the Rinks are still the projected favourite at about 780 points and 25.4% to win. Debits & Checks (771, 16.5%), PhilCap (769, 15.3%) and 97 Problems (769, 16.0%) are bunched right behind.
recap.impact: We hold a cushion of about 10 projected points, but three teams within 11 points means nothing is safe yet.

recap.text: PhilCap had the week's biggest jump among contenders: 39 points since last Monday, title odds up from 7.5% to 15.3%, and a climb from 6th to 3rd in the projections. Dom Scavuzzo went the other way, odds down from 13.7% to 8.0%.
recap.impact: PhilCap outscored us by 4 this week and are now a real threat. Dom Scavuzzo fading thins out the chasing pack.

recap.text: Poppy's Picks owned the week with 48 points, led by Mikael Granlund and Beckett Sennecke (10 each) and Jack Hughes (9). Cutter Gauthier also had 10 for RDR, and Connor McDavid added 8 for 97 Problems.
recap.impact: Poppy's jump from 13th to 6th in the real standings, but they're projected around 732, about 48 behind us, so it's not a worry yet.

recap.text: Brayden Point left Sunday's game in Winnipeg after the first period, and the Lightning said he might miss some time. Elsewhere, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (Debits & Checks) took a puck to the head Saturday, and Dylan Larkin (also Debits & Checks) remains suspended by the Red Wings until he's traded.
recap.impact: Point is a first-line, first-unit power-play centre for us, so a few weeks out would cost real points. Our closest chaser, Debits & Checks, have problems of their own with Larkin out indefinitely.

recap.text: On the power play, Dylan Holloway has dropped to St. Louis's second unit, while Porter Martone moved up to Philadelphia's first unit.
recap.impact: It roughly evens out for us: Holloway had no points this week, and Martone's bump gives our rookie a better shot at production.

lens.headline: A 35-point week kept you on top of the projections, but PhilCap are closing fast.
bullets: You're 5th in the real standings with 174 points, 8 back of PhilCap and Tage Against the Machine, and projected to finish 1st with about 780.
Win odds are 25.4%, down slightly from 26.1% last Monday, and top-3 odds are 53.3%, about the same as a week ago (53.6%).
The projected gap is about 10 points to Debits & Checks, with PhilCap and 97 Problems about 11 back. PhilCap doubled their odds this week, so matching their pace is how you keep the cushion.

Kaprizov led the way with 6 points, and Johnston, Brady Tkachuk, Point, Reinhart and Hintz added 5 each. Kaprizov (16 goals on 61 shots) and Brady Tkachuk (10 on 58) are still finishing at rates that usually cool off, while Johnston (3 on 42) is due for more.
Next week, watch Point's status after he left Sunday's game, Holloway on the second power-play unit, and whether Holloway, Sanderson and Frondell get back on the scoresheet after pointless weeks.

lens.headline: Kaprizov's hat trick kept you in a three-way race, now 3rd projected.
bullets: You're 16th in the real standings with 29 points, but projected to finish 3rd with about 737, and your roster still projects 1st in the pool from here on.
Win odds slipped from 18.7% to 17.1% since last week's recap, and top-3 odds from 40% to 39%, as Dom Scavuzzo jumped past you from 4th to 1st projected.
The projected gap to 1st is about 6 points (737 to 743). Closing it comes down to your cold shooters: Wyatt Johnston, Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk have 35 shots between them and no goals.

Kaprizov drove the week with 5 points, including a hat trick against Florida, and Dylan Holloway had a three-assist night. Kaprizov's 6 goals on 13 shots are running hot, while Frondell lost his top power-play spot and Reinhart is centring a line without Barkov.
Next week, watch Sanderson's return from his lower-body injury, whether Johnston and Reinhart finally score, and Dom Scavuzzo's Hagel and Kucherov, who had 6 points each this week.

recap.text: Chugalugs91 still lead the real standings with 76 points, ahead of Debits & Checks (59) and Peter Will Probably Pick Old Guys (58). Sebastian Aho just set a pool record with a point in six straight games. The projections still have Chugalugs91 finishing last, with a 0.1% title chance.
recap.impact: No threat to you. They lead you by 47 points today, but you're projected to finish about 99 points ahead of them.

recap.text: The title race is a three-way dead heat. Dom Scavuzzo jumped from 4th to 1st projected, with odds up from 11% to 18%. 97 Problems slipped to 2nd at 17%, and Lord of the Rinks sits 3rd at 17%. Debits & Checks are next at 9%.
recap.impact: You're right in it: about 6 projected points separate you from 1st, and the gap to 4th is about 15 points.

recap.text: Biggest movers: PhilCap fell from 3rd to 5th projected (9% to 8%) with Ivan Demidov and William Eklund both on injured reserve. Anthony Scavuzzo dropped from 11th to 14th after Travis Konecny and Mats Zuccarello went on injured reserve. In the real standings, Debits & Checks climbed from 9th to 2nd and RDR slid from 3rd to 10th.
recap.impact: Good for you. PhilCap was one of the teams projected just behind you a week ago, and now sits about 16 points back.

recap.text: Top pool scorers this week: Auston Matthews 9 points (Girl on the Lake), William Nylander 8 (Debits & Checks), and Alexis Lafreniere, Tim Stutzle and Sebastian Aho with 7 each. Dom Scavuzzo got 6 apiece from Brandon Hagel and Nikita Kucherov.
recap.impact: Hagel and Kucherov are the ones that hurt: they powered the team that just passed you. Kaprizov's 5 points led your roster.

recap.text: Role changes on your roster: Anton Frondell dropped from Chicago's top power-play unit to the second, Porter Martone moved up to Philadelphia's second line but back to the second power-play unit, and Brady Tkachuk moved onto Florida's top line. Sam Reinhart is centring Florida's second line with Aleksander Barkov out 6 to 8 weeks.
recap.impact: Small knocks for Frondell and Reinhart, who were already projected for modest totals. Martone's bigger even-strength role is a mild plus.

recap.text: Injuries: Jake Sanderson is still day-to-day with a lower-body injury and has played one game. Travis Konecny and Mats Zuccarello joined the injured reserve list, and Connor Bedard, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Mathew Barzal remain out.
recap.impact: Sanderson is the one to watch for you: he has one game played, and every game he misses is one fewer from your defence.

lens.headline: A pool-best 43-point week vaulted you to 1st in the projections.
bullets: You're 13th in the real standings with 72 points, 25 back of Chugalugs91, but projected to finish 1st with about 752.
Win odds climbed from 17.1% to 21.8% since last week's recap, and top-3 odds from 39% to 46%, as you jumped Dom Scavuzzo and 97 Problems.

You're now about 10 points ahead of 97 Problems (743) and 11 ahead of Dom Scavuzzo (742) in the projections. Holding that comes down to staying healthy, with Hintz and Sanderson the two question marks.

Brady Tkachuk (10 points), Sam Reinhart (8) and Kirill Kaprizov (7) drove the week. Tkachuk and Kaprizov are scoring on a high share of their shots (6 goals on 32, 10 on 26), so expect some cooling, while Wyatt Johnston is still looking for his first goal on 16 shots.
Next week, watch Hintz's status for Tuesday against Boston, Sanderson's return, Anton Frondell now on the second power-play unit, and Minnesota's four-game week for Kaprizov.

recap.impact: You're the team to catch now, but the cushion is only about 10 points, so one bad week could flip it.

recap.impact: Brady Tkachuk and Reinhart drove your week. McDavid's 10 keeps 97 Problems as your closest chaser.

recap.text: PhilCap had the roughest week, falling from 5th to 9th in the projections as their title odds halved from 7.7% to 3.8%, with William Eklund out 10 to 12 weeks and Ivan Demidov on injured reserve. This Is the Year climbed from 8th to 5th (6.0% to 7.8%).
recap.impact: One fewer contender near the top. This Is the Year are about 30 points back of you in the projections, not an immediate worry.

recap.text: Injuries to watch: John Tavares is on injured reserve for Debits & Checks, Taylor Hall is week-to-week for Girl on the Lake, and Just Here for the Poker are without Josh Morrissey (week-to-week) and Owen Tippett (day-to-day). Roope Hintz left Saturday's game in Chicago and is questionable for Tuesday.
recap.impact: Tavares going down hurts the 4th-place projected team, which helps you a little. Hintz is the one to worry about, along with Jake Sanderson, who has played once all season.

items.headline: Tage Against the Machine wear the crown
items.body: Tage Against the Machine sit 1st in the real standings with 188 points, edging past PhilCap.

items.headline: Jack Hughes is a point machine
items.body: Seven straight games with a point for Jack Hughes, 12 points in that stretch. Poppy's Picks are cashing in.

items.headline: Bratt keeps the engine humming
items.body: Jesper Bratt scored in Winnipeg and has 10 points over seven straight games for This Is the Year.

items.body: Title odds jump from 16% to 19%, and 97 Problems climb to 2nd in the projections.

items.headline: Suzuki keeps cashing in
items.body: Nick Suzuki scored in Montreal's overtime loss and has 9 points over six straight games for Just Here for the Poker.
